$comment: sim_core.wasm bench baseline (#254 §4). Written by hand from `node scripts/bench-wasm.mjs` — the median of 3 interleaved passes × 7 runs, Node 22 / V8 on the CI-class Linux VM this study ran on (cpp/README.md → Compile-flag study). `npm run bench:wasm -- --baseline=cpp/bench-baseline.json` (build-wasm.yml runs it on every fresh build) fails when the binary grows > 5 % (size is deterministic under the pinned emsdk) and warns when a throughput drops below 0.6× (runners differ; that bound still catches a lost SIMD kernel at 0.37× or a lost -flto). Re-baseline on purpose, with the numbers in the PR.
$size_note: Re-baselined for #256 (Circuit Lab, ADR-0018): +48 235 B raw / +18 974 B brotli, all the MNA solver (cpp/src/circuit/; ~8.5 KB of it is musl printf for error texts). Throughput rows kept: main's 74 145 B binary and this one bench within noise of each other on the same VM, so the solver costs the plants nothing.
$size_note_257: Re-baselined for #257 (calibrated twin, ADR-0019): +40 864 B raw / +12 540 B brotli (122 380 → 163 244 / 50 695 → 63 235), the EKF + Levenberg–Marquardt fit in cpp/src/twin/ (dual-number RK4 sensitivities instantiated per width) and the AD Jacobian in ros23. Throughput rows kept: main's 122 380 B binary and this one, interleaved 2 × 7 runs on the same VM, are within noise on seg / particles / fdtd / ring rk4 / ring dopri5, and ring ros23 is ~20 % faster (one dual evaluation per Jacobian instead of n + 1 RHS).
